rootCause: clean replaced only a small list of named entities and decimal ' in a chained sequence. Hexadecimal and other numeric references survived in HN titles/body, while &lt; could be decoded twice. HN refreshes also retained existing non-social body text, leaving historical malformed text unchanged.
changes: Decode recognized named references and decimal/hexadecimal Unicode scalar references in one pass after stripping actual markup. Include Latin-1 named characters for Spanish/Portuguese and common typography; preserve unknown/malformed references as evidence.
Replace null, surrogate and out-of-range numeric references with U+FFFD without throwing; keep encoded tags as literal text for existing React rendering.

Store the prior HN normalizer's output only in an ephemeral WeakMap keyed by parsed provider objects. Refresh historical body text only for the same HN source/publication when the existing body exactly equals that current provider response normalized by the old algorithm.

Preserve modified editorial annotations, status, tags, analysis, provenance, IDs and approved pieces. Opportunity fingerprints change when repaired evidence text changes and remain stable on repeated unchanged refreshes.
Add regression tests at fetchSource/syncSources and verify imported reference cards/detail interactively in the native T3 browser at desktop/mobile, including storage readback after reload.

verification.before: Original reproduction: 8 tests, 2 passed and 6 failed, including original //' symptoms, Unicode, ordinary named typography, double decoding and persisted HN text. Follow-up legacy test: 9 passed / 1 failed before the refresh repair. Latin-1 follow-up: 10 passed / 1 failed before extending named characters.
verification.after: Final suite: 11 tests passed, 0 failed/cancelled/skipped. FetchSource calls both HN modes through a controlled JSON transport; syncSources persists readable title/body, keeps one reference after repetition, repairs exact legacy body matches, preserves changed annotations and approved piece/version, and updates the opportunity fingerprint only when its evidence changes.

verification.before: Existing nearby suites preserved unchanged by this agent.
verification.after: 90 passed, 0 failed/cancelled/skipped. Provider transport, RSS, safeFetch/SSRF, analysis/draft and opportunity fingerprint behavior retained.

verification.command: Native T3 preview: own tab at http://127.0.1.33:5523/radar → Explorar → reload → Explorar; desktop 1280×800 and mobile 390×844.
verification.before: Original adversarial evidence showed hexadecimal entities literally in the HN card/detail. A synthetic HN provider payload was ingested through production syncSources, without external calls.
verification.after: Card and detail contain https://, apostrophe, ñ é 😀 🚀 and © – … €. Encoded and remain literal text; no injected image node or payload execution. Double-encoded </'/" remain encoded after one pass. UI title/body exactly match API/SQLite readback after reload, same reference ID and 47 points/8 comments; no horizontal page overflow at either viewport.

limitations: Provider responses and account/company were explicitly synthetic. No live Hacker News request, credentials, paid provider or publication was used; this verifies parsing, persistence and rendering, not live provider availability.

The named table covers XML, Latin-1 and common typography, not the full HTML5 named-entity catalog. Unsupported names and malformed references remain literal instead of being guessed or recursively decoded.

Historical correction is conservative and refresh-driven: it does not rewrite the database globally. A body that differs from the current HN response under the old normalizer is preserved, including annotations or provider text that has changed.

Piece approval versions cover editorial piece content. Refreshing evidence leaves existing piece records untouched; the separate opportunity fingerprint reflects changed evidence. This agent did not change approval policy.
Browser checks exercise the supplied encoded markup payload as React text; they do not establish a general-purpose HTML sanitizer guarantee.
No global build was run. The coordinator owns final combined build/test and compiled UI validation.
